sentences.text: Researchers developed multiVIB, a computational method using probabilistic contrastive learning to align diverse single-cell datasets.

Testing on benchmarks confirmed the approach integrates data effectively while avoiding false matches, and it was applied to nine molecular data types from mouse primary motor cortex to construct a comprehensive atlas.

The framework further integrated gene expression data from primate basal ganglia to identify shared and unique cell types, leading authors to conclude it offers a reliable way to build large-scale brain cell maps.
